Hi Lisa — thanks Naomi. I can confirm the following from a legal/ops perspective.

1) Controller vs Processor
- For the hosted API mode where Acme sends prompts and controls the downstream use of outputs, Acme is the controller and Redwood is the processor. Our standard DPA (we can provide the executed or template version) mirrors this relationship and includes processor obligations (processing in accordance with documented instructions, subprocessors, security measures). If there are any cases where Redwood makes independent decisions about purposes/means (for example, if we enrich data from other customers — rare), we'd need to re-evaluate.

2) DSR operational workflow (summary)
- Intake: Customer submits request to privacy@acmehealth.com and we intake via our portal or via a secure upload link.
- Verification: Redwood requires controller-signed attestation or records showing user identity verification (to avoid erroneous deletions).
- Execution: Upon validated request, Redwood executes an automated deletion job that removes user-identifiable artifacts from live runtime caches, object storage, and any persisted logs tied to the account ID.
- Backups & retained state: Cold backups may persist for disaster recovery; typical retention window is up to 30 days. We schedule a scrub job that removes items in backup once eligible.
- Attestation & audit: We provide a signed attestation report describing the steps taken and artifacts removed. Standard turnaround: 10 business days for routine deletion requests; 30 days for complex/archive scenarios.

3) Evidence & attestation language
- Attached is a sample deletion attestation language we provide customers. We include: request id, timestamp, scope of data removed, retention exceptions, and signature from our privacy lead. (I will prepare a redlineable template for Acme.)

4) Subprocessors & SCCs/DPA
- Karthik: can you confirm the active subprocessors for Acme's account and the executed SCCs?

Next steps: Naomi — please share anything operationally that should be documented in the attestation (e.g., KV cache flush logs, exact storage object keys pattern). Lisa — if you can confirm the format you'd like the attestation (PDF + hash, or signed PDF only), we'll produce a sample.
